title: Price and date parcel kinds the manifest has never seen

blocks.text: The shipping service prints a manifest for every van that leaves the depot: what the postage comes to and when the last parcel arrives. Today it carries `Letter`s and `Box`es. Next quarter the freight team adds crates and the courier team adds next-day envelopes, each in its own module, and they won't be editing your code to do it.

items: `totalCents(...)`: every parcel's base postage, plus 2 % of the declared value of each insured parcel, rounded up to the next cent;
`deliveredBy(...)`: the day the last parcel is delivered when they all leave on the given day.

blocks.text: When you're done, the manifest prices and dates a parcel kind written after it, by any team, without a change to `Manifest`. The tests bring kinds of their own. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: letters and boxes cost their base postage, insured boxes add 2 % of their declared value rounded up to the cent, and an empty manifest costs nothing
a manifest of letters and boxes is delivered when its slowest parcel arrives, and an empty one on the day it ships
a parcel kind written after the manifest, with no insurance, costs its own base postage
an insured parcel kind written after the manifest pays the insurance surcharge on its declared value
a parcel kind written after the manifest is dated by its own transit time, faster or slower than letters and boxes

origin.section: Put the Behaviour on the Type, and a New Type Is One New Class That javac Checks

concepts: With the behaviour on each type behind an interface, a new type is one new class that javac refuses until every operation is written, and callers run it from their unchanged class files.
A type check copied into several methods compiles when one copy misses a new type; a fallback branch answers wrongly without a sound and a throwing branch fails only when its path runs.
